concepts.title: Human Capital and Human Capital Formation
concepts.definition: Human capital formation is the process of adding skills and knowledge to the population through education, health, training, migration and information, making people a productive resource whose returns appear as higher earnings and faster growth.
concepts.key_idea: Expenditure on education and health is treated as investment in human capital because it raises future productivity, just like investment in physical capital.

concepts.title: Education Sector in India: Levels, Institutions and Expenditure
concepts.definition: Education in India spans elementary, secondary, higher and adult levels with institutions from primary schools to universities, financed by government and private spending, and literacy rates and enrolment ratios measure progress, with the Right to Education making elementary education a fundamental right.
concepts.key_idea: Government expenditure on education as a percentage of GDP and the rise in literacy rate indicate the growth of the education sector.

concepts.title: Unemployment, Human Capital and Economic Growth Linkage
concepts.definition: Human capital formation raises productivity and growth but unemployment wastes human capital; defects of the education system include low public spending, mismatch between education and jobs, brain drain and gender and regional disparities in literacy.
concepts.key_idea: The chapter stresses that without jobs, educated persons cannot deploy their human capital, weakening the education growth linkage.
